content.user_title: Plan Customer Renewals and Expansion Pricing
content.value_statement: Existing customer pricing can drift when renewal notices, upgrade triggers, and downgrade responses lack consistent policies. This skill structures value-based renewal plans, expansion recommendations, and customer-specific downgrade responses.
actual_capabilities: Draft renewal plans with renewal dates, current prices, recommended prices, delivered-value rationales, and notice paragraphs.
Flag renewals inside the 90-day notice window and recommend extending current pricing before a later change.
Compare grandfathered pricing with gradual increases of 5-15% per renewal cycle over 12-24 months.
Suggest expansion conversations based on usage thresholds, buyer changes, achieved outcomes, and adjacent-team interest.
Recommend differentiated renewal treatment for the lowest and highest customer value segments.
Build downgrade response playbooks using five questions about usage, team size, budget, delivered value, and departure intent.
limitations: Requires pricing configuration and customer records; it does not include a CRM connector or billing integration.
Provides planning guidance and draft text, not automatic price changes, customer messages, or subscription updates.
Its 90-day notice policy and suggested increase ranges are guidelines, not validated forecasts or legal advice.
The source discourages self-service downgrades; customer rights and contract terms must take priority over that recommendation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Upcoming Renewals
use_cases.description: Review customer renewal dates, identify missed notice windows, and draft value-based pricing recommendations.

use_cases.title: Define Existing Customer Pricing Policy
use_cases.description: Compare grandfathering and gradual increases while tailoring treatment to customer value segments.

use_cases.title: Assess Expansion and Downgrade Requests
use_cases.description: Use customer usage, outcomes, and account context to prepare upgrade conversations and appropriate downgrade responses.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Renewal
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this customer renewal: [date], [current price], [notice already sent], and [delivered value]. Recommend the next action and explain any notice issue.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: assess one upcoming customer renewal.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Renewal Notice
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a renewal notice using [renewal date], [current price], [proposed price], and [verified improvements]. Check the 90-day window and avoid unsupported value claims.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare customer-facing renewal text for review.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Expansion Conversations
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [customer usage, tier limits, buyer changes, and outcomes]. Identify expansion triggers, recommend upgrade paths, and state effective price impacts using [approved tier prices].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prioritize expansion conversations across several accounts.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Customer Pricing Playbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [pricing configuration] and [customer records], build renewal, expansion, and downgrade plans. Compare grandfathering with gradual increases. Flag missing notices and preserve authorized downgrades.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate pricing recommendations across the existing customer base.

output_examples.input: Example customer: renewal in 45 days, current price $500 monthly, no prior notice, and a proposed price increase.
output: Recommended action: Extend current pricing for one quarter, subject to contract review.
Next step: Send a documented notice for the next eligible pricing change.

output_examples.input: Example customer: 85% of a tier limit, confirmed reporting improvements, current price $500 monthly, and an approved upgrade price of $650.
output: Expansion trigger: Usage exceeds the 80% threshold.
Suggested expansion: Discuss the approved higher tier before the customer reaches its limit.
Effective price impact: $150 more per month.
Talking points: Explain added capacity and connect verified reporting improvements to the customer's stated outcomes.

output_examples.input: Example customer: requests a downgrade after team size decreases, while the remaining team still uses the product.
output: Diagnosis: The use case remains active, but the team requires less capacity.
Recommended response: Allow the appropriate downgrade and document the smaller use case.
Future opportunity: Revisit expansion if the team grows.
Customer protection: Do not delay an authorized downgrade to require a retention conversation.

best_practices: Provide verified renewal dates, approved tier prices, notice history, and specific evidence of delivered customer value.
Review recommended prices and notices against contracts before approving customer communications or billing changes.
Use optional downgrade diagnostics while preserving timely customer-authorized changes and minimizing shared customer data.
anti_patterns: Applying the same increase to every customer without considering delivered value, account size, or renewal timing.
Treating generated plans as permission to change billing or send notices without human approval.
Blocking an authorized downgrade until a customer completes a retention conversation.

faq.question: What information does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide pricing tiers, renewal cadence, notice history, expansion triggers, and relevant customer records. Missing information should remain explicit.

faq.question: Does it connect to our CRM or billing system?
faq.answer: No connector or billing integration is included. You must supply authorized customer data through your existing workflow.

faq.question: What does it recommend when notice is late?
faq.answer: It recommends extending current pricing for one quarter and sending proper notice for a later cycle, subject to contract review.

faq.question: Does it recommend immediate increases for every customer?
faq.answer: No. It favors grandfathering or gradual increases, with smaller changes for lower-value accounts and custom conversations for the highest-value accounts.

faq.question: How should downgrade recommendations be applied?
faq.answer: Use the diagnostic questions to understand customer needs. Do not let the source's mandatory-conversation policy delay authorized changes or override contractual rights.

faq.question: Can this skill run independently?
faq.answer: The source marks it as not directly user-invocable and routes it from a main pricing skill. Standalone behavior depends on the host tool.
